name: hook_iat_ac_ti_only
description: Cross-process IAT hook of user32!GetAsyncKeyState inside ac_client.exe. RQ3 evasion: only ETW-TI subscribed.

extra.target_selection_notes: user32.dll!PeekMessageA is the standard Win32 message-pump call, invoked every frame at 60+ Hz by any game that owns its own message loop. First attempt: user32.dll!GetAsyncKeyState — not imported (AC gets input via WM_KEYDOWN messages, not polling). Second attempt: kernel32.dll!Sleep — also not imported directly; AC gets Sleep via SDL_Delay wrapping in SDL.dll rather than a direct kernel32 import. Third attempt: user32.dll!PeekMessageA — expected to work. If it also fails, run `ProcessToolkit.exe list-imports --pid <ac_pid>` on the VM to see AC's actual imports and pick a real one. --verify-hits 0 skips the runtime-firing counter check because the frame-rate-dependent cadence varies.
extra.expected_fingerprint: PE header walk + import descriptor walk yields 6-12 small READVM_REMOTE events; 1x ALLOCVM_REMOTE (~4KB RWX); 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (trampoline write, ~4KB); 1x PROTECTVM_REMOTE (IAT page RO->RW); 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (4-byte slot overwrite); 1x PROTECTVM_REMOTE (restore). Small WRITEVM lands in ac_client.exe's IAT (parsable via pe_utils), NOT in .text — this is the distinguishing signal vs hook_inline_ac.
